Title: Morphological evolution and modularity of the caecilian skull
Rationale: Cranial modules = 16 landmark-defined skull regions whose shape covaries across 32 genera; evolutionary rate per module (cheek module fastest).

Title: Shape variation and modularity of skull and teeth in domesticated horses and wild equids
Rationale: Six cranial developmental modules from geometric morphometrics; integration compared between domesticated and wild equids.

Title: Unravelling intravertebral integration, modularity and disparity in Felidae (Mammalia)
Rationale: Intravertebral trait modules from covariance of vertebral landmarks across felids; integration vs. disparity along the column (direct analogue of the backbone example).

Title: Phylogenetic conservatism in skulls and evolutionary lability in limbs – morphological evolution across an ancient frog radiation is shaped by diet, locomotion and burrowing
Rationale: Skull vs. limb modules with different evolutionary rates/conservatism across a frog radiation.

Title: Ontogenetic changes in the phenotypic integration and modularity of leaf functional traits
Rationale: Leaf traits form defence and economy modules in juveniles; trait correlation 'interconnectivity' rises in adults. Ontogeny is the trajectory.

Title: Robustness of trait connections across environmental gradients and growth forms
Rationale: Hyper module: plant traits are the nodes of a probabilistic graphical model; modules are clusters of directly connected traits across 16k records.

Title: Comparing the strength of modular signal, and evaluating alternative modular hypotheses, using covariance ratio effect sizes with morphometric data
Rationale: Methods paper: covariance-ratio effect size to compare modular hypotheses in morphometric trait data (rodent mandibles); covers levels of organization.

Title: Modular Evolution of the Drosophila Metabolome
Rationale: Hyper module: metabolite levels are traits that coevolve across 11 Drosophila species; modules are enriched for biochemical pathways (functions) and linked to lifespan.

Title: Modularity: genes, development and evolution.
Rationale: Review of variational (trait) modularity in quantitative genetics, linked to developmental genetics and the adaptive landscape across levels of organization.

Title: Architecture of the human interactome defines protein communities and disease networks
Rationale: BioPlex 2.0 AP-MS interactome; Markov clustering gives >1,300 protein communities that map to complexes and pathways.

Title: A global genetic interaction network maps a wiring diagram of cellular function
Rationale: Global yeast genetic interaction network; profile similarity yields a hierarchy from complexes to pathways to bioprocesses.

Title: Revealing modular organization in the yeast transcriptional network
Rationale: Module networks: TF-to-gene regulatory network; modules are overlapping, condition-specific gene sets under shared regulators (regulatory programs).

Title: The modular and integrative functional architecture of the human brain
Rationale: Hyper module: rs-fMRI brain network modules, each mapping to a discrete cognitive function; connector hubs between modules.

Title: Modularity and stability in ecological communities
Rationale: Species-interaction networks; modular vs. anti-modular community matrices and local stability (random matrix theory).

Title: Macroecological trends in nestedness and modularity of seed-dispersal networks: human impact matters
Rationale: Bipartite plant-disperser networks; modularity/nestedness related to latitude, climate and human impact. Species are the elements, as in the microbial community example.

Title: Wheat rhizosphere harbors a less complex and more stable microbial co-occurrence pattern than bulk soil
Rationale: Microbial co-occurrence networks (nodes = taxa); modules, keystone taxa and topology compared between rhizosphere and bulk soil.

Title: Phylogenomic analysis of gene co‐expression networks reveals the evolution of functional modules
Rationale: Hyper module: plant co-expression network modules dated by phylostratigraphy; duplication/speciation of functional (cell wall) modules.

Title: The Evolutionary Origins of Modularity
Rationale: Simulated evolution of networks under connection cost; modularity Q emerges. Networks + evolutionary trajectory.

Title: A genome-wide atlas of co-essential modules assigns function to uncharacterized genes
Rationale: Co-essentiality (CRISPR fitness profile) gene network; modules are pathways/complexes used to assign gene function. Same design as the note's knockout-network example.

Title: Modular organization of cellular networks
Rationale: Clusters protein interaction networks into modules; identifies module-organizer and module-connector proteins.

Title: Modular Cell Biology: Retroactivity and Insulation
Rationale: Transcriptional components with input/output; retroactivity (loading) breaks modularity, and insulation restores it.

Title: Resource Competition Shapes the Response of Genetic Circuits
Rationale: Gene cassettes composed into circuits; shared transcriptional/translational resources couple modules (same theme as the ribosome-demand example).

Title: A Load Driver Device for Engineering Modularity in Biological Networks
Rationale: Load driver device insulates upstream gene module from downstream load (timescale separation), restoring input/output behaviour.

Title: Carboxysomes: metabolic modules for CO2 fixation.
Rationale: Carboxysome as a CO2-fixation function module; protein-domain building blocks organized in genetic loci (nested objects); plug-and-play engineering.

Title: The Origins and Evolution of Functional Modules: Lessons from Protein Complexes
Rationale: Protein complexes as functional modules in PPI networks; origins by duplication and co-option (evolutionary trajectory).

Title: An immediate–late gene expression module decodes ERK signal duration
Rationale: Immediate-late gene expression module turns ERK signal duration (input) into gene expression (output).

Title: Combinatorial assembly and design of enzymes
Rationale: Enzyme fragments are combinatorially assembled into functional endoxylanases; modules nested in the enzyme. Weakest fit to the three axes.

Title: A spectrum of modularity in multi‐functional gene circuits
Rationale: Multi-functional gene circuits; asks whether functions map to separable sub-circuits (hybrid) or are emergent (non-modular).

Title: Transcriptional Architecture of Synaptic Communication Delineates GABAergic Neuron Identity
Rationale: Hyper module: combinatorial expression of gene families (adhesion, receptors, channels) shapes synaptic input/output and defines neuron types as individuals with traits. Analogue of the LRR example.

Title: Evolution of Bow-Tie Architectures in Biology
Rationale: Bow-tie (multi-layer) networks evolved to meet an input/output goal; metabolism and signaling are examples.
